decisions.reason: As a multi-model extension of the core office range that fits the firm's stated move toward flexible workplace solutions, the desk system benefits from sunk development effort and is likely to be defended rather than withdrawn.

The chair family is close to the established business and supports the firm's broad interior offering, so management is likely to continue it and interpret any weaker results as temporary rather than abandon it quickly.

Although more niche, the floor-cushion line still builds on the firm's interior concept and existing material expertise, and the investment in several models makes management somewhat reluctant to cut it.
The upholstered sofa sits squarely in the firm's design-led living and lounge identity and was publicly launched with strong messaging, which raises commitment to keeping it in the range.

The high standing table is a close fit with evolving office and conference use cases, so despite only moderate visibility management would likely retain it as part of the flexible-workplace direction.

Because the rug collection was presented as a flagship for the firm's strategic direction, public commitment and sunk costs make management especially prone to continue backing it even if performance has been mixed.
